_source: Roy's words that are not in the manuscript. Latest October 11: standalone idle replaces the idle: prefix; on the couch remains historical writing; the old key is retained so saved references and the editor stay valid. "on the bus" is from his October 4 screenshot and October 6 mockup; "watching tv", "pacing", "waking up", "trying to sleep" and "reading a magazine" were supplied for the archived phone experiment (September 28-29); "happy" is from his October 6 mockup; "lying on the couch" is from his October 7 message ("the game begins with the description lying on the couch"); "shopping for groceries" is from his October 7 message ("buy groceries should queue activities (on the bus, shopping for groceries, etc)"); "content" and "troubled" are moods from his October 7 message ("sometime it will say stuff like content or troubled while sleeping"); "thought:" and "bills" are from his October 7 sketch of a thought card ("thought: / bills") and message ("thinking about bills would give you some info on that"). Copy exactly; never add a label Roy hasn't supplied.
_presentTense: Roy, October 7: "activities are in present tense". The labels below marked in `provisional` are Claude's present-tense forms of the manuscript's action labels: only the verb changes, every other word, spelling and punctuation is kept ("go to the hole" becomes "going to the hole"; until Roy took the full stop out of the card on October 18, 395, it was "go to the. hole" and "going to the. hole"). Roy confirmed the form on October 7 ("all activities should be like 'on the bus' 'pacing' etc"); the individual wordings are still Claude's until he approves or rewords them. The cards still use the manuscript's labels as written.
_moods: The mood words in `moods` are Claude's, written at Roy's request (October 7: "yes create a lot of other mood words along these lines", after "happy", "content" and "troubled"), kept to plain, everyday mood words ("hollow isn't a great mood word don't use words like this. simpler words describing moods"). They wait for his approval or rewording. Roy, October 11: "don't use gloomy anymore", so "gloomy" is removed.
